title: A new name after trouble
question: After a business is barred or suspended, has its licence suspended, or has its registration closed, does a newer name in the same owner-group go on being paid?
finding: 1 newer payee names are tied to a troubled one: 1 to an organization on the City’s suspended and debarred lists, 0 to a firm whose State contractor licence is shown as suspended, and 0 to a registration the Treasurer closed. The largest: KM 106 Construction Inc., paid $1,811,649 since, tied to Azul Works, Inc (5: same address only). 1 older affiliates that were already City payees more than a year before the action are left out, as is the one row already shown in the site’s “People and roles” page. 30 listed organizations and 16 payees with a suspended licence were tested; for a suspended licence the tied firm is listed only if its own licence was issued, or its City payments began, after July 2019.
how: Three kinds of trouble are taken from records: the City’s Suspended and Debarred Contractors page and semi-annual reports (with the action date); a State contractor licence shown as suspended in the November 2026 licence file; a business registration marked closed by the Treasurer. For each troubled name, every other City payee tied to it is listed: in the same owner-group (tiers 1 to 4), at the same suite-level address (tier 5), or carrying a State-numbered person who left the troubled firm’s licence and is on the other one. A row is kept only if the other name was registered or first paid no earlier than a year before the action and was paid at least $10,000 afterwards. Payments are split at the fiscal year of the action.
limits: A shared address is not shared ownership, and a licensed person changing firms is ordinary; neither shows that the newer firm stands in for the older one. A suspended firm may finish contracts it holds. Most licence suspensions in the State file are labelled as a bond or workers’ compensation insurance lapse; the State file leaves out revoked and cancelled licences, so the worst cases cannot appear. A closed registration followed by a new one under the same owner is usually a reorganization. The project’s case files are not used as a trigger: being named in the file of a case is not being a party to it, and nothing here says that any organization in this table is charged with or convicted of anything. The State’s officer and agent filings would settle most rows.

columns.t: Registered with the City (business registry; a State incorporation can be earlier)

rows.what: On the City’s Suspended and Debarred Contractors list, shown there as “Agreed not to seek new City contracts”
rows.evidence: Azul Works Inc. and KM 106 Construction Inc. were registered at the same address (1400 block of Egbert Ave) from 2022-01-01 to now; 4 owners ever registered there
